task: Write one sentence of your own using the word limpid. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know limpid should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The portrait's limpid green eyes seem lit from behind, and visitors swear they follow you.
Clean means free of dirt but says nothing about seeing through; it stops well short of limpid.
Clear goes further than clean, yet stops short of limpid, which is so transparent it hardly seems to be there.

Crystalline means clear as cut crystal — a close twin, sharing the see-through purity. Limpid adds ease and beauty: the transparency feels effortless, like spring water, and it carries into eyes, voices, and prose. Crystalline stresses the hard, faceted brilliance; limpid stays soft and still.

Glassy describes a surface smooth and still as glass — a claim about the top alone, saying nothing about what lies beneath. Limpid is the opposite claim: you see straight through, the whole depth clear. A pond can be glassy at dawn and still hide everything beneath the surface.
so clouded nothing shows through
stirred thick with sediment

Latin limpa may be a cousin of lympha, the clear-water word behind 'lymph,' but scholars call that link only probable — and no other common English word grew from limp- itself. So limpid stands essentially alone, one word holding the root's whole clear stream.
Limpid means clear, transparent.
Reviewers keep praising the translator's limpid English: sentences you look straight through to the meaning, with nothing clouded and nothing showing off.
Limpid is stronger than plain 'clear' because it suggests a beautiful, effortless transparency — the quality of spring water carried over to eyes, air, voices, or prose.
Writing can be clear yet clumsy; limpid writing is clear the way still water is.
Limpid flatters whatever it touches — water, eyes, a singing tone, prose — by making clarity beautiful.
Don't confuse it with limp (drooping); the two are unrelated.
And keep it apart from this unit's manifest: limpid describes the medium you see through, manifest the fact that stands in plain view.

What set him apart, the judges wrote, was a limpid tone: every note seemed to arrive without effort, nothing strained and nothing showy.
